title: infer baseline metrics from perf artifacts and canonicalize affordance tags
author: Priya Kulkarni
description:
Motivation: onboarding new model variants currently requires manual baseline entry and ad-hoc affordance tags, which leads to stale performance claims and tag explosion in the registry. This PR provides two coordinated automations: (1) an extractor that reads standard perf artifacts (CSV/JSON) produced by the benchmark lab and computes resilient baselines (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-token estimates) which are recorded in the model metadata; (2) an affordance normalizer that collapses synonym tags into a canonical set and writes alias mappings to preserve provenance. Also adds a lightweight changelog blurb generator that synthesizes human-friendly release notes for baseline changes so downstream consumers can detect behaviour shifts.

What this changes: a new baseline inference library (registry/baseline), a normalization table and reconciliation logic (registry/affordance), a small cli command (cli/mr ingest-baseline), a perf artifact CI hook that triggers ingest on artifact publish, unit+integration tests, docs and an onboarding example. The baseline extractor is defensive: it validates artifact schema, requires a minimal sample size to accept automated baselines, and records confidence metrics so reviewers can opt for manual review for low-confidence cases.

Implementation notes: - Baseline algorithm: aggregate sample-level latency/throughput measurements into percentiles using t-digest, compute cost-per-token using provided cost model and quantization profile. Output is a compact JSON blob stored under model.metadata.baselines.v1 with provenance fields (source_artifact_sha, computed_at, confidence).
- Affordance normalizer: we maintain a canonical affordance set (chat,instruct,embed,rerank,code,translate) and a synonym-to-canonical mapping that is editable via the registry UI. On ingest, synonyms are stored under metadata.affordance_aliases while the canonical tag is added to metadata.affordances.
- Changelog summarizer: simple templating + highlight rules (e.g. >10% p95 regression flagged as "notable"), emits a one-paragraph blurb suitable for release notes and the model history timeline.

Testing and rollout: added unit tests for the t-digest based percentile computation, integration tests that run the ingest CLI against fixture artifacts, and a perf smoke test that compares auto-baseline to an existing manual baseline to guard against large deltas. Feature gated behind MR_FEATURE_AUTO_BASELINE; rollout is behind a server-side flag and the ingest will create a draft change that requires a registry maintainer to approve for final write by default.

Backward compatibility: old affordance tags are preserved in alias lists; code reading affordances continues to check metadata.affordances as before. Automated baseline writes add a versioned key (baselines.v1) and do not overwrite any manually authored baseline unless the maintainer explicitly approves the merge.

Related: complements ENG-8421 (onboard cadence) and PM-1149 (improve release notes visibility).

review_comments: Ethan Moore: Please add a unit test that simulates skewed latency distributions (long tails) and validates percentile stability.
Priya Kulkarni: Added test for synthetic long-tail distributions and documented t-digest tradeoffs in registry/baseline/tdigest.py header.
Lena Fischer: We should not auto-publish a baseline if confidence < 0.7. Can we gate it behind a review step?

Priya Kulkarni: Ingest now records confidence and creates a draft model-change for confidence < 0.8. Maintainers can approve via the registry UI. Updated docs to explain the threshold and how to override.

tests: perf-regression-check: pass (auto-baseline vs manual baseline within tolerance for fixtures)
release_notes: Auto-baseline: model registry can now extract canonical performance baselines from benchmark artifacts and attach them to model metadata (p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost-estimates). Affordance normalization: synonyms are collapsed into a canonical affordance list while aliases are preserved. An automated changelog blurb is produced for baseline changes. Feature gated and can be configured in the registry console.
migration_instructions: Run migrations/2025_11_14_affordance_aliases.sql to create the affordance alias table. If you have existing manual baselines, run the CLI 'mr migrate-manual-baselines --preview' to generate draft baseline documents for review. Default confidence threshold is 0.8; change via MR_FEATURE_AUTO_BASELINE_CONF in the feature flags service.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. Computation of percentiles uses t-digest and is robust for large samples, but we guard by confidence thresholds and draft workflows to avoid accidental overwrites. Primary risks: malformed artifacts (schema validation added) and mapping errors for affordance synonyms (editable mapping and alias preservation mitigates).
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the ingest safety checks (schema validation, minimal sample size, confidence calc) and the affordance mapping defaults. The summarizer is intentionally simple; if you want richer language we can iterate separately.
